context:
Small, mechanical port: copy nightly.yml:205-220 (reachability wait) and
nightly.yml:222-236 (all-skipped grep guard) into pr.yml's
postgres-integration job, adjusting only for the two pytest invocations
that exist there (live integration tests, then the TPC-Havoc equivalence
sample) versus nightly's single invocation. No shared script extraction
needed for this scope - keep the two workflow files independently
readable.
description:
`nightly.yml`'s live-postgres job has two anti-skip guards
(nightly.yml:205-236): one that fails outright if the service container
never becomes reachable (so `skip_unless_docker_service` cannot silently
green a required gate), and one that greps the pytest summary line for
`N passed` so an all-skipped run cannot pass either. Neither guard exists
in `pr.yml`'s `postgres-integration` job. That job is already
`continue-on-error: true` (pr.yml:552) and explicitly documented as a
non-blocking second-engine equivalence SAMPLE (pr.yml:550-552,
pr.yml:587-591), so this item does not propose making it blocking. The
problem is narrower: today, "service never came up, 0 tests ran" and
"service came up, tests ran and passed" both render as a green
`continue-on-error` check with no visible distinction, so a silently
all-skipped sample looks identical to a real pass in the PR checks UI.

anti_patterns.dont: add the guard only to the first pytest step and skip the TPC-Havoc equivalence step
anti_patterns.why: an all-skipped equivalence sample is exactly the kind of silent gap this item exists to close

anti_patterns.dont: extract the guard into a shared composite action or script in this pass
anti_patterns.instead: inline copies are fine at this scale.
anti_patterns.why: the two call sites differ (one vs two pytest invocations) and a premature abstraction risks under-covering the second

anti_patterns.dont: flip continue-on-error to false as part of this change
anti_patterns.instead: keep this item scoped to visibility only.
anti_patterns.why: that's a separate blocking-promotion decision with its own stability bar (see graduate-browser-smoke-to-blocking-gates.yaml for the pattern such a promotion should follow)

preserves.behavior: The DuckDB SQL correctness-gate job remains the sole hard blocker for SQL correctness, per pr.yml:550-552, 610-611, 650-651 comments.
nightly.yml's own anti-skip guard (nightly.yml:205-236) is left untouched; this is a back-port, not a refactor of the shared logic into one place.

postgres-integration stays continue-on-error: true - this item does not promote it to a blocking gate (that's a separate, larger decision given the job's own comment calling it a non-blocking sample, pr.yml:550-552).

prior_art.concept: nightly.yml:222-236 tee + grep all-skipped guard — reuse pattern, apply to two call sites instead of one

verifications.command: Temporarily misconfigure the postgres service port in a scratch branch's pr.yml, open a PR, observe the postgres-integration check
verifications.description: Job fails visibly (while staying non-blocking) when postgres never becomes reachable
verifications.expected: postgres-integration shows failed/red in PR checks (continue-on-error keeps ci-required-result green)

verifications.command: On a scratch branch, temporarily add ` -k this_matches_nothing_zzz` to the postgres-integration pytest invocation in pr.yml (do NOT rename/move test_postgresql_live.py -- scope_limit.do_not_modify forbids touching that file), open a PR
verifications.description: Job fails visibly when the pytest invocation collects zero items
verifications.expected: postgres-integration fails on the all-skipped grep guard, not silently green

verifications.description: Normal PR still passes the sample with a real green
